summary: Lookout tower above Nadina Lake on a 3.3 km trail with camping amenities; a Houston Hikers trail map whose file name dates it to April 2012 says it is no longer manned. No build history found.

access.note: Houston Hikers presents the trail and camping spot as a day hike and camp, and mentions no closure or permit requirement. The guide shows no date.

visit.trail_note: 3.3 km trail, 3 to 3.5 hours round trip, with its trailhead along the Old Tahtsa (Washout) FSR; no cell coverage. Site includes a lookout tower, outhouse, room for tenting, spring cot, and propane stove and fridge.

events.note: Houston Hikers trail map says the lookout is no longer manned. The April 2012 date comes from the file name only; the PDF text carries no date

evidence.supports: Lookout situated above Nadina Lake; a moderate day hike or a camping spot
evidence.quote: Situated above Nadina Lake the lookout provides and moderate day hike or a great spot for camping.

evidence.supports: Trailhead along the Old Tahtsa (Washout) FSR
Distance from Houston given as 60 km or more
Directions give about 110 km from Houston
Distance from Houston given as 124 km on the trail map
Lookout no longer manned, on the trail map (file name dated April 2012)
Site amenities include a propane stove and fridge

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The guide header gives 60 km or more, its directions give about 110 km, and its trail map gives 124 km. The story reports all three without choosing one.
Firelookout.ca gives 53.86954, -126.97775; the web index gives 53.863, -126.943. The two are about 2.4 km apart (computed from the two coordinate sets); the story reports both.
The guide page says Moderate, and the trail map says Easy. Not used in the story.

sources.title: Dina (Dena)
sources.publisher: Canada Lookouts (web index of Canadian lookouts)

notes_for_editor: No build date, builder or fire history was found in readable sources. The Houston Hikers guide page is undated. The trail map is the source for the no-longer-manned statement; its April 2012 date comes from the file name only, because the PDF text carries no date, so the story attributes the date to the file name. The Houston Hikers guide and map disagree on distance from Houston and on difficulty; both are reported above. The story gives the elevation as 1,304 m (4,278 ft), converted from the index's metre figure. The Firelookout.ca record has no description, height or build data. Read budget was used up on this lookout before its history could be checked further. Not read: a campingmap.ca listing and a Facebook group post, both found in search.
